title: Choose the passive
instructions: Read the active sentence. Then tap the pendulum with the verb form that completes it in the passive.

rounds.active: The new firm is designing our head office in Lisbon.
rounds.note: The active is present continuous (is designing), so the passive keeps it: is being + past participle.

rounds.active: They built the bridge in 1998.
rounds.note: A finished past time (in 1998) needs the past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

rounds.active: Somebody cleans the offices every evening.
rounds.note: A routine (every evening) is present simple; plural offices, so are + past participle.

rounds.active: They will announce the results tomorrow.
rounds.note: Will + be + past participle. 'Will announce' is still active — the results don't announce anything.

rounds.active: They are going to open a new school next year.
rounds.note: Keep 'going to' and add be + past participle: is going to be opened.

rounds.active: They were repairing the road when we arrived.
rounds.note: The repair was in progress when we arrived: past continuous passive, was being + past participle.

rounds.active: Someone has stolen my bike!
rounds.note: A past action with a result now (the bike is gone): has/have been + past participle.

rounds.active: By six o'clock they had cleaned the whole house.
rounds.passive: By six o'clock the whole house ___.
rounds.note: 'By six o'clock' marks a point in the past before which it was done: had been + past participle.

rounds.active: The builders will have finished the stadium by May.
rounds.note: 'By May' looks back from a future point: will have been + past participle.

rounds.active: You must wear a helmet on the building site.
rounds.passive: A helmet ___ on the building site.
rounds.note: Modal + be + past participle. 'Must wear' is active; 'must being' is never possible.

rounds.active: They can't finish the project on time.
rounds.note: Can't + be + past participle. After a modal the verb is always the bare form: be, never been or being.

rounds.active: Someone should have told us earlier.
rounds.note: A past criticism: should have been + past participle. The person told is now the subject.

rounds.active: They might have cancelled the concert.
rounds.note: A guess about the past: might have been + past participle.

rounds.active: A mechanic is going to check my car.
rounds.passive: I'm going to ___ my car checked.
rounds.note: Have + object + past participle: someone else does the job for you — I'm going to have my car checked.

rounds.active: The hairdresser cut my hair yesterday.
rounds.note: Past causative: had + object + past participle. 'I cut my hair' would mean you did it yourself.

rounds.active: People say that he is a millionaire.
rounds.note: People say (now) → he is said; the belief is about now, so 'to be'.

rounds.active: People believe the painting was stolen in 1990.
rounds.passive: The painting ___ to have been stolen in 1990.
rounds.note: The belief is now (is believed); the theft was earlier, so 'to have been stolen'.

rounds.active: They speak Portuguese in Brazil.
rounds.note: A general fact is present simple: is + past participle. Portuguese doesn't speak — people speak it.

rounds.active: A lot of tourists visit the castle every year.
rounds.passive: The castle ___ by a lot of tourists every year.
rounds.note: Every year → present simple passive. Keep 'by' when the agent (a lot of tourists) matters.

rounds.active: They didn't invite Jack to the party.
rounds.note: Didn't invite (past simple negative) → wasn't + past participle.

rounds.active: Did someone lock the door?
rounds.note: A past simple question in the passive starts with was/were: Was the door locked?

rounds.active: They won't repair the lift until Monday.
rounds.note: Won't + be + past participle. The lift can't repair anything, so 'won't repair' is impossible.

rounds.active: Someone is following us!
rounds.note: Happening right now → present continuous passive: are being + past participle.

rounds.active: They are going to demolish the old cinema.
rounds.note: Going to + be + past participle keeps the plan and makes it passive.

rounds.active: The police arrested three men last night.
rounds.note: Three men is plural, and 'last night' is finished time: were + past participle.

rounds.active: They make these watches in Switzerland.
rounds.note: Plural subject (these watches) → are + past participle.

rounds.active: Were they painting the house when you called?
rounds.passive: ___ the house being painted when you called?
rounds.note: The new subject is 'the house' (singular), so was — not were, which belonged to 'they'.

rounds.active: They haven't answered my email yet.
rounds.note: 'Yet' goes with the present perfect: hasn't been + past participle.

rounds.active: Has anyone seen my keys?
rounds.note: My keys is plural, so have: Have my keys been seen?

rounds.active: By the time we arrived, someone had eaten all the cake.
rounds.passive: By the time we arrived, all the cake ___.
rounds.note: Done before a past moment → past perfect passive: had been + past participle.

rounds.active: They have just renovated the old market.
rounds.note: Just goes between has and been: has just been + past participle.

rounds.active: Someone had warned them about the storm.
rounds.note: Keep the tense of the active: had warned → had been warned.

rounds.active: They will have sold all the tickets by Friday.
rounds.note: By Friday looks back from the future: will have been + past participle.

rounds.active: Nobody has cleaned this room for weeks.
rounds.note: Nobody has cleaned → it hasn't been cleaned. 'For weeks' keeps the present perfect.

rounds.active: You can't use your phone during the exam.
rounds.note: Modal + be + past participle: can't be used.

rounds.active: We should water the plants every day.
rounds.note: Advice about now → should be + past participle. 'Should have been' would be about the past.

rounds.active: They may cancel the flight because of the fog.
rounds.passive: The flight ___ because of the fog.
rounds.note: A possibility now or later → may be + past participle.

rounds.active: You have to fill in this form in capital letters.
rounds.note: Have to works like a modal: has to be + past participle. This form is singular, so has.

rounds.active: Someone could have hurt the child.
rounds.note: A past possibility that didn't happen → could have been + past participle.

rounds.active: They must have left the door open.
rounds.note: A confident guess about the past: must have been + past participle.

rounds.active: You needn't wash these shirts by hand.
rounds.note: Needn't + be + past participle: it isn't necessary.

rounds.active: They ought to repair the roads before winter.
rounds.note: Ought to keeps its 'to': ought to be + past participle.

rounds.active: A photographer is going to take our wedding photos.
rounds.passive: We're going to ___ our wedding photos taken.
rounds.note: Have + object + past participle: someone else takes the photos for us.

rounds.active: Someone is repairing my laptop at the moment.
rounds.passive: I'm ___ my laptop repaired at the moment.
rounds.note: In progress now → I'm having it repaired.

rounds.active: The dentist checked my teeth last week.
rounds.passive: I had my teeth ___ last week.
rounds.note: After have + object comes the past participle: had my teeth checked.

rounds.active: A decorator has painted our living room.
rounds.note: Present perfect causative: we've had + object + past participle.

rounds.active: Somebody stole her bag on the bus.
rounds.passive: She had her bag ___ on the bus.
rounds.note: Have + object + past participle can describe something bad that happens to you: she had her bag stolen.

rounds.active: A mechanic should service your car every year.
rounds.passive: You should ___ your car serviced every year.
rounds.note: After a modal, the bare verb: should have your car serviced.

rounds.active: I'll ask a tailor to shorten these trousers.
rounds.note: Get + object + past participle is the informal causative: I'll get them shortened.

rounds.active: Did someone deliver the pizza for you?
rounds.note: After did, the bare verb: Did you have it delivered?

rounds.active: People think that the minister will resign.
rounds.note: People think (now) → is thought; the future action becomes 'to resign'.

rounds.active: People say that the hotel was built in 1850.
rounds.passive: The hotel ___ to have been built in 1850.
rounds.note: Saying is now (is said); the building was earlier (to have been built).

rounds.active: People believed that the ship had sunk.
rounds.note: The belief was in the past (believed), so was believed.

rounds.active: It is reported that the storm is getting stronger.
rounds.passive: The storm ___ to be getting stronger.
rounds.note: Something in progress now → is reported to be getting.

rounds.active: People expect that prices will rise again.
rounds.note: Prices is plural → are expected to rise.

rounds.active: People know that he has lived abroad.
rounds.note: Knowing is now (is known); the living abroad came before (to have lived).

rounds.active: They say the singer is working on a new album.
rounds.passive: The singer ___ to be working on a new album.
rounds.note: They say (now) → is said; still happening → to be working.

rounds.active: People considered him the best player in the team.
rounds.passive: He ___ the best player in the team.
rounds.note: Considered (past) → was considered, with no 'to be' needed after consider.
